claims.visible_claim: This page places Openness to Experience—curiosity, imagination, and receptivity to new experience—within the Big Five continuous-domain framework ([S1](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2283588/)). The six facets below use NEO/IPIP-NEO vocabulary. The official IPIP resource says its scales measure constructs similar to NEO facets, while the BFI-2 uses a different 15-facet architecture ([S11](https://ipip.ori.org/Finding_Scales_to_Measure_Particular_Constructs.htm); [S2](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27055049/)). These labels must not be treated as fully equivalent across instruments.
claims.boundary: Supports a continuous domain and labeled NEO/IPIP-NEO vocabulary, not scale equivalence or FermatMind product validity.

claims.visible_claim: Openness and cognitive ability are different constructs. A large-scale meta-analysis found that relationships vary by personality level—domain, aspect, or facet—and by the type of cognitive ability being examined. That evidence cannot be compressed into “Openness equals intelligence” or used to predict an individual’s IQ from an Openness result ([S10](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2212794120)).
claims.boundary: Group-level associations do not equate Openness with intelligence or predict one person's IQ.

claims.visible_claim: FermatMind has not published product-level reliability, validity, Chinese norms, or individual predictive evidence for the scores discussed by this package. This material is for self-observation and education. It is not for clinical diagnosis, hiring screening, school admission, or replacing a career decision.
claims.boundary: Public product and method boundary; not an empirical research claim.
